requirements.requirement: Serve DNSSEC-signed infra.test authoritatively with node1 as primary and node2/node3 as secondaries.
requirements.summary: Final checks show node1 active and enabled as a secure inline-signing primary, while node2 and node3 are active secure secondaries at the same signed serial 2026090206. DNSKEY and RRSIG records are served authoritatively.

requirements.requirement: Publish app.infra.test as node1's service address and status.infra.test as TXT ready.
requirements.summary: Node1's observed address is 10.100.102.10, and final authoritative responses from the primary and both secondaries return app.infra.test A 10.100.102.10 and status.infra.test TXT "ready", with signatures.

requirements.requirement: Configure node4 to resolve infra.test through both secondaries.
requirements.summary: Node4's persistent NetworkManager profile and resolv.conf contain both secondary addresses. Normal resolution used node2, the outage test used node3, and the two-server configuration and signed resolution persisted after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Accept authenticated updates from node1 and propagate changes to both secondaries.
requirements.summary: A TSIG-keyed update from node1 was accepted and advanced the serial; the signed test record and matching serial appeared on both secondaries. An unkeyed update was refused. The authenticated cleanup advanced the serial again to 2026090206 and propagated to both secondaries.

requirements.requirement: Keep resolution available when one authoritative server is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A healthy two-secondary baseline was observed, node2 was then stopped with its DNS listener absent, and node4 successfully resolved required and newly updated signed data through node3. Node2 was subsequently restored active with the current serial and data.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct, coherent final-state and transition evidence. DNSSEC topology, required records, dual-secondary resolution, authenticated update propagation, bounded failover and recovery, and provider-wide restart recovery are all demonstrated without contradiction.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, protected TSIG material, BIND configuration, firewall rules, service enablement, and node4's DNS profile were necessary implementation actions. The temporary update record was bounded verification and was removed; the node2 outage was restored. Reboot scheduling was required by the provider protocol. Final lifecycle observations show healthy package state, no failed services, and only the intended DNS listeners. The restart protocol is complete and coherent on every node: each has healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, recovered service/data or resolver state, and fixed lifecycle boot identities that corroborate the transition.
